steps.instructions: Answer the operator's question about the code in scope, READ-ONLY. Change nothing: create, edit or delete no file in any repository, commit nothing, and run no command that writes there; every write to the code is refused in this step (the one place the boundary admits is this step's own notes directory, scratch outside every repository, and the answer needs none). GROUND FIRST: query the code graph through the wicked-garden-search skill and the read-only estate shim, one call per lookup in your shell: "$WICKED_GARDEN_ROOT/scripts/wicked-garden" run scripts/_estate_client.py --readonly call '{"tool":"SearchEntity","arguments":{"name":"<symbol>"}}' (outside a crew run the launcher is `wicked-garden`). The same form reaches BlastRadius and Lineage ({"symbol":"<name>"}) for who depends on what and where data flows, RankHotspots ({"limit":20}) for the load-bearing code, the skill's path action for how A reaches B, and knowledge.recall (the wicked-garden-mem skill) for recorded decisions. Always pass --readonly. THEN CONFIRM: open and read every file you cite, at the lines you cite, before you cite it. ANSWER: lead with the answer in plain words, then the evidence. Every claim cites what it rests on: a file and line relative to its repository root and prefixed with the repository name (`alpha/src/foo.ts:42`), a symbol (`alpha::Foo::bar`), or a graph path from the shim (`a -> b -> c`). A claim you could not ground is named as such in one line, never asserted. NOT INDEXED: only when no code graph is bound for a repository in scope (the scope statement says no code graph is bound, or the shim says it has no store to read), say so in the answer's first line: `<repository> is not indexed: this answer reads the files directly and may miss callers. Index this repository to ground answers in its code graph.` Then answer from the files. A bound graph that finds nothing for a symbol, or one lookup the shim refuses, is not that: say which lookup came back empty or refused (the symbol may be newer than the last index), keep using the graph for the rest, and confirm that part from the files. A follow-up question in this conversation is answered the same way. A request for a change is not attempted: say what would change and where, cited, and that a job, not this analysis, makes changes.
